Given that 
$$
\displaystyle C=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & q & 5 \\ 0 & -4 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$ 
and $det(C)=59,$ find the value of $q.$

Expand along the first row, using the signs $+,-,+$. Compute the three signed contributions separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1} & =(2)\begin{vmatrix}q & 5 \\ -4 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(2)((q)(1)-(5)(-4)) \\  & =(2)(q + 20) \\  & =2 q + 40\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{2} & =-(3)\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-(3)((-1)(1)-(5)(0)) \\  & =-(3)(-1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{3} & =(1)\begin{vmatrix}-1 & q \\ 0 & -4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1)((-1)(-4)-(q)(0)) \\  & =(1)(4) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Add the signed contributions to obtain the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =T_1+T_2+T_3 \\  & =2 q + 47\end{aligned}
$$

Set the determinant equal to the given value.

$$
\begin{aligned}2 q + 47 & =59 \\ 2 q & =12 \\ q & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $q=6$.
